author: pk910
content:
We've recovered devnet-9 after an unplanned un-finality this morning and we're planning to shut it down at EOD if nothing valuable is left to do with it.
Please take a look at your client nodes, especially those still being offline.

We had two (unplanned) unfinality events in the network, the first caused by an incompatible prysm image, and the second due to a collective restart of all lighthouse nodes. We could restore finality both times, so we call it a success 🙂

The general performance is a bit alarming. During the unfinality period, all major CL clients (prysm, lighthouse & teku) struggled to keep up with the head. We've seen repeated OOM kills on 32G machines. The devnet-9 state was twice the mainnet state with equal active key count, so clients should be able to handle this load to be safe for real mainnet incidents. So, I think there's some improvements to be done 😉

We didn't have to take any special action to restore finality. The clients eventually caught up and the chain recovered on its own. So while there's definitely room for improvement, the current state isn't a death sentence for recovery during an actual mainnet incident.

Shout out to lodestar and nimbus, who stayed alive during the unfinality periods and did their duties fine.

author: taratorio
content: instead of switching watchtower off maybe we can have it deploy once a day?

author: nflaig
content: I am really not a fan of having uncontrolled restarts, I do have alerts set up so I know any time lodestar misses a block but if it's just because a unlucky restart right before the proposal it's just wasted time to look into those, having a dedicated branch to merge like `glamsterdam-devnet-8` from which I can essentially trigger a redeploy myself by just rebasing it against unstable is much better, that way it also takes ~15-30 mins to rollout a new image without requiring anyone from ethpandaops side. I do understand why we wanna run trunk branches, but in our case, the devnet branch is literally the same code

author: taratorio
content: i see your point. on the other hand it is quite nice to have our latest code changes tested and rolled forward automatically via CD so that we can catch bugs sooner. maybe you can improve your alerts to be smarter and corelate missed block timings to restart timings? once a day should not be too noisy

author: nflaig
content: yeah my alert could be smarter, but also this allows me to roll out new code changes faster, rather than slower, I am actually just in the process of rebasing the glam 8 branch now against unstable, if we did the "deploy once a day from trunk" strategy I would have to wait until that event happens or bother someone from pandaops to trigger a rollout

author: taratorio
content: yea true, sounds like what would be ideal is "once a day auto roll forward" + "on demand roll forward" (like the `/build-client-<el/cl>` command we have in <#892088344438255616> )

author: nflaig
content: `"once a day auto roll forward"` I dislike anything that restarts the node uncontrolled, it also skews the metrics (ie. can hide memory leaks or alike), I feel like this is only useful if I don't care about the devnet or wanna pay 0 attention to it myself and wait for someone else to catch a bug for me that a auto-rollout caused. ` "on demand roll forward"` that seems nice to have

author: taratorio
content: personally i like CD for this environment and would prefer to have it. if you dont like it then you should have the option to opt out.

author: nflaig
content: I think CD is more useful for early devnets, I want lodestar to be mainnet ready and be tested in a similar manner to how we test our mainnet release candidates, in our case you can even run our latest release v1.47.0 already on any glamsterdam devnet. I just don't think it's useful to do CD for us at this point, we haven't had a major issue since like 5 devnets ago, at this point, we wanna find performance bottlenecks that will cause slightly lower head vote % or other such issues, and this requires good metrics to build up, which restarts skew with

author: taratorio
content: that makes sense. you should be able to opt out then.
